summary: Phase 1 Task 2 (Document Upload progress + guardrails) verified. TypeScript compile clean (exit 0). Metro bundling clean (only pre-existing shadow*/expo-notifications/RNGoogleSignIn warnings — all acceptable per spec). Static inspection of constants/upload.ts, services/drive.ts, contexts/VaultContext.tsx, app/upload/file.tsx, and app/upload/review.tsx confirms all spec items. E2E on web (viewport 420x900) went splash → login-demo-btn → onboarding-continue-btn → tab-add-fab → upload-category-Insurance → pick-sample-btn → upload-continue-btn → details-continue-btn → review-submit-btn; upload fails at FileSystem.getInfoAsync on web (expected), the error banner surfaces with review-error-dismiss, submit button flips to 'Retry upload', and pressing it again re-triggers addDoc without crashing the app. Retry pathway validated.

e2e_flow.review_submit_btn_first_attempt: failed-as-expected on web (FileSystem.getInfoAsync unavailable); local-fallback path also failed at same getInfoAsync; uploadError banner surfaced with review-error-dismiss present
e2e_flow.review_submit_btn_retry: re-triggered addDoc, same expected failure, no crash — app remains interactive with retry-upload button and dismiss control

critical_code_review_comments: Local-fallback branch in VaultContext.addDoc still calls saveEncryptedLocal, which internally invokes FileSystem.getInfoAsync (unavailable on web). So on web BOTH the primary Drive path and the local fallback fail with the same UnavailabilityError. That is per web-preview limitation and correctly surfaces via error banner + retry, but on-device this fallback is fine. If web-preview UX matters, gate the local fallback with Platform.OS !== 'web' or catch that specific error before invoking saveEncryptedLocal.

uploadProgress is not reset back to 0 on success (before navigation) or on retry press — minor: the progress box remains hidden by the (uploadProgress > 0 && < 1) guard, so no visual glitch, but consider setUploadProgress(0) on clearUploadError or on submit-retry for clarity.

xhrMultipartUpload sends a string body via XHR — for large multipart payloads with base64 ciphertext this keeps everything in memory and does not stream. Fine for the 50 MB cap; reconsider when resumable path is wired up.
test_credentials: Demo login via login-demo-btn (no creds required).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Task 2 of Phase 1 fully verified. Web-preview cannot exercise the true success branch of addDoc because expo-file-system.getInfoAsync is unavailable on web; the error banner + retry pathway is the intended surfacing and it works. Next: Task 3 of Phase 1.
rca of the issue: N/A — all Task 2 spec items met.
